feature_insights.headline: BBMP city study extent and stressed groundwater setting

insights.explanation: Study frame is defined between 12.833 to 13.142 N and 77.462 to 77.786 E, covering 711 sq km BBMP.
insights.title: Defined BBMP extent

insights.explanation: Wet year range shifts from pre 2.51 to 163.51 m bgl to post 2.00 to 135.15 m bgl with 72.04% rise and 27.96% fall, contrasting drought year pre 4.1 to 85.5 m bgl to post 3.19 to 92.6 m bgl with 15.9% rise and 84.1% fall.
insights.title: Interannual water level contrast

insights.explanation: Extraction stage is 242.08% with recharge 91.89 MCM and extraction 200.21 MCM, categorized as overexploited.
insights.title: Overexploited balance

feature_insights.summary: Bengaluru City BBMP study area lies between 12.833 to 13.142 N and 77.462 to 77.786 E, covering 711 sq km.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Map frame of BBMP boundary to locate aquifer, supply and scarcity overlays.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Same extent hosts extraction stage 242.08% with recharge 91.89 MCM against extraction 200.21 MCM, framing scarcity and supply stress.

feature_insights.headline: Weathered phreatic aquifer forming shallow unconfined zone

insights.explanation: Weathered depth median is 19.35 m with IQR 10 to 30 m and range 1.15 to 58.4 m.
insights.title: Weathered zone thickness

insights.explanation: Urban depth to water is 1 to 5 m bgl in unconfined weathered aquifer.
insights.title: Shallow urban water table

feature_insights.summary: Aquifer-I is the city-wide weathered phreatic aquifer with median depth 19.35 m and IQR 10 to 30 m.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Shallow weathered column above fractured bedrock to show unconfined storage.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: It provides shallow unconfined storage with urban levels 1 to 5 m bgl, sensitive to paving and recharge change.

feature_insights.headline: Fractured aquifer with productive interval at mid depth

insights.explanation: Fracture share is 30% in 0 to 50 m, 52% in 50 to 100 m, 13% in 100 to 150 m and 5% in 150 to 200 m, making 50 to 100 m the most productive interval.
insights.title: Fracture depth distribution

feature_insights.summary: Aquifer-II is the city-wide fractured and jointed rock aquifer, most productive in 50 to 100 m bgl with 52 percent of fractures.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Depth bar highlighting mid-depth fractured interval beneath weathered cover.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Productivity concentrates in fractured rock, so yields depend on fracture presence rather than uniform depth.

feature_insights.headline: Peninsular Gneissic basement defining hard-rock setting

insights.explanation: Basement is Peninsular Gneissic Complex of Archean 2500 to 3500 mya with Closepet granite averaging 4 km width and Gabbro Dolerite Norite Pyroxenite intrusions.
insights.title: Archean gneissic basement

feature_insights.summary: City basement is Peninsular Gneissic Complex, Archean 2500 to 3500 mya with Closepet granite and basic intrusions.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Basement block underlying weathered and fractured aquifer zones.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Hard crystalline basement controls weathering depth and fracture flow, shaping foundations and borewell behavior.

feature_insights.headline: Red laterite soil controlling surface intake

insights.explanation: Infiltration rate in Red Soil is 2.4 to 8.2 cm/hr, with higher intake where permeable cover remains.
insights.title: Measured infiltration range

feature_insights.summary: Dominant red lateritic soil shows infiltration rate 2.4 to 8.2 cm/hr over saprolite.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Soil surface with intake gradient from paved to open ground.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Intake capacity links rainfall to shallow recharge, explaining runoff increase where cover is sealed.

feature_insights.headline: Piped network with partial coverage and large asset file

insights.explanation: KML holds 97827 features with 95138 LineString and 2689 without geometry, with empty name and description in samples.
insights.title: Network asset size and gaps

insights.explanation: Demand is 2676 MLD against supply 1893 MLD leaving deficit 783 MLD, with Cauvery 1450 MLD plus groundwater 746 MLD plus Stage-V 300 MLD and UAW 705 MLD.
insights.title: Demand supply imbalance

feature_insights.summary: BWSSB water supply lines network holds 97827 features with 95138 LineString and 2689 without geometry.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: City line map with density contrast between inner fully covered and outer partially covered zones.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Partial coverage forces borewell dependence, linking supply deficit to overexploitation and scarcity.

feature_insights.headline: Phase 3 Corridor 3-1 elevated alignment and shallow ground profile

insights.explanation: Corridor length is 32.15 km with 22 stations, fully elevated double-decker viaduct shown schematically.
insights.title: Corridor scale

insights.explanation: Program drilled 36 boreholes to 30 m at about 1000 m spacing with 150 mm dia and SPT every 3 m, showing 0 to 10 m cohesionless soil over moderately strong to strong rock.
insights.title: Investigation and ground model

feature_insights.summary: Bengaluru Metro Phase 3 Corridor 3-1 is 32.15 km with 22 stations, fully elevated double-decker, schematic only.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Elevated alignment trace over soil-over-rock column to flag pier investigation needs.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Length and station spread set land, utility and foundation interfaces in PGC terrain.

feature_insights.headline: Phase 3 Corridor 3-2 shorter elevated spur

insights.explanation: Corridor length is 12.50 km with 9 stations, fully elevated double-decker viaduct shown schematically.
insights.title: Corridor scale

feature_insights.summary: Bengaluru Metro Phase 3 Corridor 3-2 is 12.50 km with 9 stations, fully elevated double-decker, schematic only.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Shorter elevated trace linked to Corridor 3-1 for interchange context.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Shorter spur still requires pier-specific checks where overburden thickens.

feature_insights.headline: GSI cluster showing sharp lateral heterogeneity

insights.explanation: Exploratory well depth is 202.3 m with SWL 140.84 m bmp and yield 3.75 lps, contrasting shallow fracture at 22 to 23 m and deep fracture at 195 to 196 m.
insights.title: Deep versus shallow fractures

feature_insights.summary: GSI Campus cluster shows EW depth 202.3 m with SWL 140.84 m bmp and yield 3.75 lps, set against shallow and deep fractures.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Cluster of closely spaced wells with divergent levels to stress local variability.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Nearby wells tap different fracture systems, so productivity cannot be extrapolated across short distances.

feature_insights.headline: T.C. Palya tracer site in granitic gneiss

insights.explanation: Site lies in PGC granitic gneiss area and supports piston-flow recharge inference without new hydraulic claims.
insights.title: Recharge test setting

feature_insights.summary: T.C. Palya tracer test site is in PGC granitic gneiss area for rainfall recharge study.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Point marker for injection site within basin context.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Geology-specific recharge helps explain why gneiss and granite areas respond differently.

feature_insights.headline: GSI tracer site in Closepet Granite

insights.explanation: Site lies in Closepet Granite and supports piston-flow recharge inference without new hydraulic claims.
insights.title: Recharge test setting

feature_insights.summary: GSI tritium injection site is in Closepet Granite for rainfall recharge study.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Point marker for granite-hosted injection site.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Granite-hosted result complements gneiss sites to show lithology control on recharge.

feature_insights.headline: Bannerghatta separation from metro alignment

insights.explanation: Shortest separation is 7.05 km from Line 3-2, with text value 7.1 km, and park area approx. 260.51 sq km.
insights.title: Distance and park size

feature_insights.summary: Bannerghatta National Park vicinity is 7.05 km from Line 3-2 southern end with area approx. 260.51 sq km and no direct overlap.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Buffer view showing park well outside alignment corridor.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Separation indicates no direct footprint, focusing attention on urban ecology rather than protected-area impact.

feature_insights.headline: Eastern and southeastern scarcity zone

insights.explanation: Zone covers 238 sq km across 52 wards where post-monsoon levels exceed 50 m bgl and seasonal fall exceeds 5 m.
insights.title: Scarcity delineation

feature_insights.summary: Groundwater scarcity vulnerable zone covers 238 sq km with 52 wards in eastern and southeastern Bengaluru.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Shaded scarcity pocket in east and southeast to target management.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: It concentrates deep levels and large falls where supply augmentation and regulation matter most.

feature_insights.headline: Cascading lake recharge system

insights.explanation: Series A recharge is 1.07 MCM per year and Series B is 1.90 MCM per year, totaling 2.97 MCM per year at 1.44 mm per day.
insights.title: Cascade recharge volumes

feature_insights.summary: Lake cascade recharge system provides Series A 1.07 MCM per year and Series B 1.90 MCM per year.
feature_insights.visual_takeaway: Linked lake chains showing distributed recharge contribution.
feature_insights.why_it_matters: Cascading filling turns treated water and lake storage into measurable shallow recharge.

limitations: Metro alignments are schematic and approximate, requiring pier-specific investigation before construction use.
BWSSB KML includes features without geometry and empty attributes, limiting hydraulic or service-level inference.
Seismic descriptions preserve conflicting zone statements without reconciliation.
Groundwater fluoride narrative and tabulated values conflict and remain unresolved.
Scarcity and yield zonations are interpretive and sensitive to monitoring density and thresholds.
